Description: tenants table (name, slug, status, plan) plus tenant_id on every Onyx table from the first migration. Onyx tables live in the onyx_app Postgres schema so the Laravel port keeps public untouched.
Acceptance_Criteria: Every Onyx table has a NOT NULL tenant_id; no table can be created without one

Description: Deny-all baseline, FORCE RLS, and a tenant predicate on every policy using onyx.current_tenant(). Service-role remains the only write path.
Acceptance_Criteria: A JWT for tenant A reads zero rows belonging to tenant B, proven by e2e

Description: Add tenant_id to the access token and to requireAuth. Reject any token without one. Tenant resolution on login from the user's membership.
Acceptance_Criteria: A token minted for one tenant cannot act on another; missing claim is a 401

Description: Roles per tenant (student, faculty, exams, placement, admin) via a memberships table so one person can hold different roles in different institutions.
Acceptance_Criteria: Role checks resolve per tenant, not globally

Description: audit_logs capturing actor, tenant, action, entity, before/after and ip for sensitive operations across academics, assessment and finance.
Acceptance_Criteria: Grade changes, role changes, fee edits and result publication all leave an audit row

Description: Create a tenant, seed its roles, invite the first admin. Tenant switcher for users who belong to more than one.
Acceptance_Criteria: A new institution is usable end to end without touching another tenant's data

Description: Role-aware shell for student, faculty, institution and exams/placement views with the tenant in context.
Acceptance_Criteria: Each role lands on its own home with only its own navigation

Description: Academic structure: programs, semesters, batches and the courses mapped into them. This is what makes the catalog institutional rather than a marketplace.
Acceptance_Criteria: A course belongs to a program and semester; a learner belongs to a batch

Description: Structured catalog with self-service and administrator-driven enrollment, including bulk enrolment by batch.
Acceptance_Criteria: Both self-service and admin-driven enrolment work; bulk enrols a whole batch

Description: Modules and lessons with streaming video, documents and resumable playback. Ports the proven player and progress engine from the port.
Acceptance_Criteria: Playback resumes at the last position; progress is per learner

Description: Downloadable resources per lesson with access control and signed, expiring URLs.
Acceptance_Criteria: A non-enrolled learner cannot obtain a signed URL

Description: Sessions per course meeting with manual roster marking and per-learner status (present, absent, late, excused).
Acceptance_Criteria: Marking a roster records one row per learner with an auditable actor

Description: Rotating QR code per session that a learner scans to mark themselves present, with a short validity window.
Acceptance_Criteria: An expired or reused code is refused; a learner cannot mark another learner

Description: Per-learner and per-cohort attendance percentages, shortfall flags and export.
Acceptance_Criteria: Percentages match a hand calculation on a seeded cohort

Description: Assignments with instructions, attachments, deadlines, late policy and a weighted rubric.
Acceptance_Criteria: A rubric's criteria weights sum to the assignment total

Description: Learner submission with file upload and resubmission rules, faculty grading against the rubric, structured feedback and return.
Acceptance_Criteria: A late submission is flagged by policy; returned feedback is visible to the learner only

Description: Draft autosave for assignment text so a dropped connection never costs a learner their effort.
Acceptance_Criteria: Killing the tab mid-answer and returning restores the draft

Description: Monaco-based multi-language editor with syntax highlighting, run controls, stdin panel and an interactive console.
Acceptance_Criteria: Editing, running and reading output works for every supported language

Description: Self-hosted Judge0 or equivalent with CPU, memory, wall-clock and network limits. Provider chosen in discovery; the interface is provider-agnostic.
Acceptance_Criteria: A fork bomb, an infinite loop and a network call all fail safely inside limits

Description: Durable queue for runs and grading so a class of 200 submitting at once degrades in latency, not in correctness.
Acceptance_Criteria: 200 concurrent submissions all complete; none are lost or double-graded

Description: Visible and hidden test cases, partial scoring, per-case results and instant feedback.
Acceptance_Criteria: Hidden test inputs are never returned to the client, proven by e2e

Description: Problems organised by topic, difficulty and tags, with progressive hints and worked solutions released on rules.
Acceptance_Criteria: A solution is only released once the configured rule is met

Description: Multi-file workspaces with snapshots, restore and mentor review comments.
Acceptance_Criteria: A snapshot restores the exact file tree it captured

Description: Reusable banks with tags, difficulty and multiple question types, versioned so an edit cannot alter a sat paper.
Acceptance_Criteria: Editing a question after an attempt does not change that attempt's paper

Description: Scheduled windows, per-attempt timers, sections, randomised selection and shuffling, and server-authoritative time.
Acceptance_Criteria: A client clock change cannot extend an attempt

Description: Answers persist as they are given so a dropped connection or refresh resumes the attempt where it left off.
Acceptance_Criteria: Killing the tab mid-attempt and returning resumes with answers intact and the timer correct

Description: Camera and screen capture with consent, plus tab-switch, focus-loss and paste detection.
Acceptance_Criteria: Every monitored event produces a reviewable record with a timestamp

Description: Flag scoring, an invigilator review queue and a per-attempt integrity timeline.
Acceptance_Criteria: An invigilator can accept or dismiss each flag, and the decision is audited

Description: Objective auto-scoring plus rubric-based subjective grading with anonymised marking.
Acceptance_Criteria: Marks are reproducible; the grader cannot see the candidate's name when anonymised

Description: Second marking, moderation and a publish step that freezes results.
Acceptance_Criteria: Results are invisible to learners until published, and publication is audited

Description: Score reports, difficulty and discrimination per item, and cohort benchmarking.
Acceptance_Criteria: Item statistics match a hand calculation on a seeded cohort

Description: CSV and PDF exports of results for faculty and institutional stakeholders.
Acceptance_Criteria: An export of a large cohort completes without timing out

Description: Verifiable certificates with unique credential IDs and a public verification page. Reuses the port's proven certificate engine.
Acceptance_Criteria: A credential verifies publicly and exposes no personal data beyond the holder's name

Description: Skills derived from completed courses, assessments and Code Lab evidence, each traceable to what earned it.
Acceptance_Criteria: Every skill on a profile links to the evidence that produced it

Description: A published, explainable formula over attendance, assessment, practice and projects, with the breakdown shown to the learner.
Acceptance_Criteria: The learner can see exactly why their score is what it is

Description: Employer records scoped to the institution, with contacts and an invitation flow.
Acceptance_Criteria: An employer sees only what the institution has shared with them

Description: Job posts with eligibility rules, learner applications, shortlisting and status tracking.
Acceptance_Criteria: An ineligible learner cannot apply; eligibility is computed, not typed

Description: Drive scheduling, rounds, attendance and offer recording.
Acceptance_Criteria: A drive's rounds and outcomes reconcile with the offers recorded

Description: Timed events with team formation, live leaderboards and structured judging, built on the Code Lab evaluator.
Acceptance_Criteria: A leaderboard is correct and stable under concurrent submissions

Description: Scheduling, structured feedback forms and optional recording, reusing the port's booking and Jitsi session model.
Acceptance_Criteria: A learner cannot see another learner's feedback

Description: Personalised progress, streaks and next-best-action nudges driven by real signals rather than a static list.
Acceptance_Criteria: The nudge changes when the underlying signal changes

Description: Per-course threaded discussion with mentions and resolution marking. Reuses the port's forum model.
Acceptance_Criteria: A resolved thread is visibly resolved and still searchable

Description: Escalation from a thread to a mentor, and a support ticket path with SLA visibility for unresolved questions.
Acceptance_Criteria: An escalated question reaches a named owner and its age is visible

Description: Programs, batches, faculty allocation and the institutional console that ties them together.
Acceptance_Criteria: An institution can run a term without touching the database

Description: Timetable construction with room and faculty clash detection, published to learner and faculty views.
Acceptance_Criteria: A double-booked room or faculty member is refused with the clash named

Description: Exam calendar with clash detection against timetables and other exams.
Acceptance_Criteria: A learner is never scheduled for two exams at once

Description: Hall capacity, seat allocation and printable seating plans and attendance sheets.
Acceptance_Criteria: Every candidate has exactly one seat and no seat is double-allocated

Description: Marks entry with moderation, grade computation and transcript generation.
Acceptance_Criteria: A transcript reconciles with the marks behind it, and generation is audited

Description: Fee heads, per-programme structures, instalments, invoices and receipts.
Acceptance_Criteria: An invoice's lines reconcile to the fee structure that produced it

Description: Gateway payment against invoices with idempotent fulfilment and reconciliation reporting. Reuses the port's payment engine.
Acceptance_Criteria: A replayed webhook never double-credits an invoice

Description: Guardian accounts linked to learners with attendance, results and fee visibility, plus notifications on key events.
Acceptance_Criteria: A guardian sees their own children only, and nothing a learner has not consented to share

Description: Adversarial cross-tenant testing across every route and table, plus an automated check in the gate.
Acceptance_Criteria: A deliberate cross-tenant attempt fails on every route, and the check runs in CI

Description: Role-by-route matrix test for student, faculty, exams, placement, admin and guardian.
Acceptance_Criteria: Every route has an asserted expectation for every role

Description: Keyboard support, visible focus, reduced-motion handling and contrast, with automated and manual audits.
Acceptance_Criteria: Key journeys pass an automated audit and a keyboard-only walkthrough

Description: Grading, proctoring and notification work moved onto durable queues with retries, dead-letter handling and visibility.
Acceptance_Criteria: A worker crash loses no work; retries are bounded and observable

Description: Load test the assessment, attendance and Code Lab paths at the stated scale and fix what it finds.
Acceptance_Criteria: 1000 concurrent learners sustained within agreed latency targets

Description: Structured logging, metrics, uptime checks and alerting on grading, proctoring and payment failures.
Acceptance_Criteria: A failed grading run pages someone before a learner reports it

Description: Backup schedule, restore rehearsal and a written recovery procedure for academic records.
Acceptance_Criteria: A restore is rehearsed end to end and the RPO and RTO are measured, not assumed

Description: Role-based UAT scripts, administrator guide, ADR index and API documentation.
Acceptance_Criteria: An institution can complete UAT without a developer in the room
